description: Raw WebGPU rendering framework layer — src/main.ts drives navigator.gpu directly with a real render pipeline, plus vertex+fragment WGSL.

buildHints.whenToUse: Any product that needs the raw WebGPU API — custom renderers, engine internals, novel rendering techniques (deferred, cluster-forward, raymarching), or shader-driven art where three.js abstractions get in the way. Pick threejs-game instead if you want a batteries-included 3D scene graph.
firstSteps: Run `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173 with HMR; open Chrome 113+, Edge 113+, or Safari 18+; a gradient triangle fills the canvas.
All rendering logic is in `src/main.ts`: adapter → device → canvas context → render pipeline → render loop → resize handler.
The shader is `src/shaders/main.wgsl` containing both the `@vertex` and `@fragment` entry points. Extend by adding vertex buffers for real geometry or uniform buffers for camera/time.
To add a textured quad next: create a GPUTexture, upload via `queue.copyExternalImageToTexture`, bind a GPUSampler + texture in a new bind group, then sample in the fragment shader.
Run `pnpm build` to emit static assets to `dist/` — deploy to any static host. WebGPU requires HTTPS in production (localhost is exempt).
gotchas: WebGPU is Chrome/Edge 113+ and Safari 18+ stable. Always feature-detect `navigator.gpu` and show a fallback UI — Firefox requires `dom.webgpu.enabled`.

The canvas format from `getPreferredCanvasFormat()` differs by platform (bgra8unorm on macOS, rgba8unorm elsewhere) — store it once and use it in both `context.configure({ format })` AND `pipeline.fragment.targets[0].format`; a mismatch throws at pipeline creation.
Each frame must call `context.getCurrentTexture().createView()` — the texture is recycled by the swap chain and stale views throw on the next submit.
Canvas resize: set `canvas.width`/`canvas.height` to `innerWidth * devicePixelRatio` (cap DPR at 2) and re-call `context.configure()` — ignoring this gives blurry output.
Always cancel `requestAnimationFrame` in the HMR dispose callback — WebGPU does not garbage-collect GPU resources and dangling frames will eventually crash the tab.
Call `shaderModule.getCompilationInfo()` during development — a broken WGSL module otherwise produces a silent black canvas.
architectureNotes: Create the GPUDevice once per page — `requestDevice()` is expensive; reuse the device for every pipeline and buffer.
Pre-create pipelines, bind group layouts, and buffers outside the render loop; only command-buffer construction belongs inside `requestAnimationFrame`.
For multiple render passes (shadow + main + post), batch into a single GPUCommandEncoder and `queue.submit` once per frame — each submit has a non-trivial CPU/GPU sync cost.

placeholders.description: WebGPU render bootstrap — device, canvas context, pipeline, render loop, resize handling. Extend by adding vertex buffers for real geometry, uniform buffers for camera/time, and textures via `queue.copyExternalImageToTexture`.
Vertex + fragment WGSL. The vertex stage emits a gradient triangle from @builtin(vertex_index). Replace positions with a vertex buffer binding for real meshes.
